# Understand quantitative studies and carry out your own analyses

QMSBR---*Quantitative Methods for Social and Behavioral Research*---is a modular collection of chapters designed to support various quantitative and statistical courses.
Its modular design serves several courses at once: each course chooses its
own route through one canonical set of chapters whose identities and links
stay stable, so a correction to a chapter improves every route that uses it.
The chapters help readers make sense of quantitative studies, following how a
study turns a question into evidence and a bounded answer. They also help
readers carry out analyses in which design, statistical reasoning,
interpretation, and reproducible computing stay connected.

The material is organized in parts. Each part opens with a short
**introduction**, keeps a **concept reference** to consult while reading, and
presents its **chapters** in reading order. **Part One** covers foundations,
regression, and generalized linear models; **Part Two** covers factor analysis
and structural equation modeling. The **R support** pages run R in the
browser, with nothing to install.

To start, read a part introduction and then its first chapter.

## Using QMSBR in a course {#using-in-a-course}

Each course chooses its own route and sequence through the chapters. A course
system such as Moodle holds the term schedule, announcements, classroom notes,
and assessment, while this site holds the chapters themselves and carries no
course-specific material. Chapter identities and links stay stable, so a
course can cite a chapter page and rely on reaching the current version of it.
[Using QMSBR in a course](about.qmd#courses), on the About page, sets out the
division in more detail.

## How to use this site

**Read online, or download the PDF.** Every chapter, introduction, and concept
reference can be read online or downloaded as a PDF, and both are built from
the same source. The web page
adds a responsive layout, a table of contents, search, and selectable code;
the PDF suits printing and annotation. The PDF link sits beside each page's
title in the collections above.

**Keep the concept reference open while reading.** Each part gathers its
central concepts, symbols, and notation in a concept reference. Read a chapter
for the lesson, and open the concept reference when you meet a term or a
symbol and want its meaning and the chapter that explains it.

**Try an analysis on the R support pages.** The R support pages carry a live R
session in the browser, so you can run a chapter's analysis, change it, and see
what changes without installing anything. The data sources page says where
each dataset comes from and on what terms it can be reused.

**Read the argument-based approach the chapters share.** The chapters read a
quantitative study as a question, the evidence and reasons that support an
answer, and the limits of that answer.
[The Argument-Based Approach](argument-approach.qmd) summarizes this reading,
and Part One Chapter 1 develops it in full.
